title: Track more Posit packages, repos and sites
description:
This PR extends `velocirepo.toml` with the Posit packages, repos and Plausible sites it was missing, and removes repos that aren't worth tracking. It's a first pass at #13, but doesn't fix it: there's still nothing that keeps the list up to date as new repos and packages appear. ## What was done A coverage audit (kept out of this repo) compared the config with: - **GitHub:** every public repo of posit-dev, rstudio, tidyverse, r-lib, tidymodels, mlverse and quarto-dev, plus the package repos of r-dbi, r-hub and sparklyr, and the own accounts of the people on opensource.posit.co. Forks are never included. - **CRAN:** CRAN's package database, matched to repos by their URL and BugReports fields, plus packages maintained from an @posit.co or @rstudio.com address. - **PyPI:** the `pyproject.toml`, `setup.py` and `setup.cfg` files in those repos, checked against PyPI's project metadata. - **Plausible:** the analytics snippets on each project's site, limited to the sites our `PLAUSIBLE_TOKEN` can read. - **#13's signal:** CRAN packages whose DESCRIPTION lists Posit or RStudio as copyright holder or funder (`cph`/`fnd`). All 378 such packages were checked. Every suggestion that adds one was preselected, and 10 more from outside the audited orgs and people were added: knitr, xaringan, servr, reactable, bindr and bindrcpp, and partner integrations such as mlflow and rsparkling. The partner integrations are tracked by CRAN downloads only, without a `github` target, because their repos are the partners' own projects. Left out on purpose: curl, community packages that credit Posit (skimr, gdtools, fpp3, tidyxl, …) and small packages that copied a Posit template. Each suggestion was reviewed by hand. The accepted ones were applied as text edits, so the config's comments and layout stay as they were. velocirepo loads the result, and every shared target still has a keeper. ## Changes to `velocirepo.toml` Projects: 466 → 959. - **582 new projects:** 230 package repos in the Posit orgs, 109 other repos there with stars or a Plausible site, 215 from Posit people's own accounts, 18 to consider (package repos of r-dbi, r-hub and sparklyr, and two archived package repos), and 10 #13 packages from elsewhere. - **120 updated projects:** 85 CRAN packages, 32 PyPI packages and 5 Plausible sites that were missing (for example reticulate, connectapi, htmltools, shinylive, quarto-cli and air-formatter). Three repos moved: - `mcp-repl`: posit-dev/mcp-repl → posit-dev/mcp-console - `orbital-r`: posit-dev/orbital → tidymodels/orbital - `rstudio-conf`: rstudio/rstudio-conf → posit-dev/posit-conf `orbital`'s duplicate entry now points to `orbital-python`. The `[data_dict.keep.github]` entry for posit-dev/orbital is gone, since `orbital-r` no longer tracks that repo. - **89 removed projects:** tracked repos with nothing but GitHub (no CRAN, PyPI or OpenVSX package, Plausible site or website) that are archived or have no stars. Their history is already collected. In total, 494 CRAN packages, 67 PyPI packages and 96 Plausible sites are added. New projects without a `github` target: `azuremlsdk`, `mlflow`, `rsparkling`, `tfio`. ## GitHub repos added (578)

title: Run the nightly fetch through velocirepo's gate
description:
Rolls out velocirepo's gate (v1.1.0 and later), per velocirepo's `docs/design/2026-10-devrel-io-rollout.md`:

- The nightly run moves from 06:00 to 09:30 UTC, an hour after yesterday ends in US Pacific time, and runs `posit-dev/velocirepo@v1` in `mode: gate`: it checks the night's data before committing it, archives the responses that can't be fetched again as release assets, and keeps a tracking issue. It only reports for now (`gate` unset); enforcing comes after two quiet weeks.
- Manual runs can `release`, `discard` or `repair` data.
- `velocirepo-heartbeat.yml` (12:30 UTC daily) checks that the nightly run happened; `velocirepo-digest.yml` (Mondays 13:30 UTC) summarizes the week.
- `velocirepo/checks.toml` accepts the known false positive `952675f07b21`: two bot comments in the same second in `events/github/positron/2026-10-02.jsonl`.
- `[settings] owners = ["jeroenjanssens"]` assigns the tracking issue.

`velocirepo check` on today's data reports nothing besides the accepted finding.

title: Describe the data for velocirepo's data dictionary
description:
The `[data_dict]` section, project `notes` and `duplicate_of` say what velocirepo 1.2.0 can't know when `velocirepo export --data-dict` describes devrel-io's data for devrel-agent:

- which project keeps a target that more than one project tracks (`duplicate_of` on the legacy ids shiny, py-shiny, orbital and pointblank; `[data_dict.keep]` for posit-dev/orbital, posit/shiny and shiny.posit.co)
- the content types the opensource.posit.co feeds set
- the two Plausible collection eras, which overlap on 2026-06-22, with `site_traffic`, `traffic_metric` and `pageviews`, `visitors` and `visits` over both
- CRAN's 17 missing days, the reactions backfill of 2026-07-27, and what tags, positron, tidyverse, posit and open-source-website are

Every note was checked against the data of 2026-10-20; the ones of devrel-agent's hand-written dictionary that the data repair of 2026-10-20 made wrong (no stars, lost GitHub history, CRAN month-ends) are left out. velocirepo 1.1.0 ignores these keys; 1.2.0 loads and validates them, and the generated dictionary passes `data-dict validate-spec` without warnings.

title: Repair data affected by the October correctness review
description:
Repairs the data affected by the bugs fixed in posit-dev/velocirepo#4, following the runbook in its fix plan, plus problems found along the way. Each source is its own commit, and each commit message has the details and checks.

## What's repaired

- **CRAN:** 87 missing month-end days, January to September 2026. CRAN itself has no data for 2025-08-25/26 and 2025-08-29 to 09-02.
- **PyPI:** 2026-06-10 for six packages. Older gaps are past PyPI's retention.
- **Plausible:** re-fetched 2026-06-22 to 10-16. This fills 2026-06-22, corrects plotnine's partial days, and replaces sampled shiny-python values. The first attempt (ee4cf305e) hit a pagination bug that duplicated and skipped rows; 576d15c33 redoes it with the fix.
- **GitHub events since 2026-06-23:** 16,270 closes, merges, comments and other events that were missed.
- **positron, quarto and rstudio:** all their events before 2026-06-23 were lost in the full re-fetch of 2026-07-28 (03f2f5e66), because the comment listing hit GitHub's 300-page limit. They're restored from each repository's start, and the yearly counts match GitHub's search.
- **Stars:** since July 2026 GitHub only lists stargazers to admins and collaborators, so no stars were stored. `daily_stars` now comes from GitHub's star history endpoint for all 465 projects, and summed `daily_stars` match the star counts within 4 stars.

## Checks

- `validate-data` reports one duplicate in `events/github/positron/2026-10-02.jsonl`. That's a false positive: two bot comments on #16390 posted in the same second.
- No files are deleted, and no stored records were lost apart from the corrections listed in the commits.

## Before merging

Some of the fixes are in posit-dev/velocirepo#5, which isn't merged or released yet. The nightly workflow installs the latest release, so until there's a release with #5 it won't record stars and can't re-fetch large repositories. The data in this PR doesn't depend on it, though. The nightly run commits to `main` every day, so merging soon avoids conflicts.

title: Add Buzzsprout podcast download fetcher
description:
This PR adds a fetch-buzzsprout.py script that adds a buzzsprout source with the-test-set as a project. It downloads two daily metrics:

* downloads: total downloads for the day
* n_episodes: total episodes published as of that day (e.g. count of all published episodes)

The raw buzzfeed data has a finer grain (e.g. app used to listen, episode-level downloads, etc..), so it is rolled up during extract / load. The transform roll up the no-op used by some other sources.
